title_en: Xiamen Yuanchang Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. v. Hainan Yuexin Group Co., Ltd. — dispute over an entrustment contract
ruling_gist_en: Both debts being due is one of the positive conditions for the formation of the statutory right of set-off. This condition not only means that both debts have become due for performance, but also requires that the time periods from the due date of performance to the expiration of the statute of limitations for each of the two debts shall overlap. In the overlapping part of the aforesaid time periods, both claims are in a performable state without defenses such as the statute of limitations. The condition that 'both debts are due' is satisfied. Even if the active claim has exceeded the statute of limitations at the time of exercising the right of set-off thereafter, it does not affect the fulfillment of this condition.

full_text_en:
Xiamen Yuanchang Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. v. Hainan Yuexin Group Co., Ltd. — dispute over commission contract

【Ruling Summary】

Both parties' debts having become due is one of the positive conditions for the formation of the statutory right of set-off. This condition not only means that both debts have reached their respective performance periods, but also requires that there be an overlapping period between the time when each debt's performance period begins and the time when the statute of limitations expires. Within this overlapping period, both claims are in a performable state without defenses such as prescription. The condition that "both parties' debts have become due" is satisfied. Even if the active claim has already become time-barred at the time the right of set-off is exercised thereafter, this does not affect the establishment of such condition.

Because the defense of prescription for the passive claim may be voluntarily waived by the party concerned, when examining the positive conditions for the formation of the right of set-off, the focus should be on the statute of limitations for the active claim. That is, if, before the statute of limitations for the active claim expires, the passive claim enters its performance period, it should be considered that the condition of both debts having become due is satisfied; conversely, the condition shall not be deemed as having been satisfied.

The exercise of the right of set-off is different from its formation. As a right of formation, the exercise of the right of set-off is not subject to the statute of limitations. Chinese law does not impose a statutory exclusion period on the exercise of the statutory right of set-off. Where the statutory right of set-off has been validly established, and no unreasonable delay exists in its exercise, the people's court should uphold the validity of the set-off, taking into account factors such as substantive fairness and the security function of the right of set-off.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court
(2018) Zui Gao Fa Min Zai No. 51

Applicant for Retrial (Plaintiff at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Xiamen Yuanchang Real Estate Development Co., Ltd., domiciled at Unit A, 38/F, No. 253 Hubin South Road, Siming District, Xiamen City, Fujian Province.
Legal Representative: Hou Chaoyang, Executive Director of the Company.
Agent ad litem: Yang Shaoyong, lawyer of Fujian United Faith & Simplicity Law Firm.
Agent ad litem: Chen Xuanwen, lawyer of Fujian United Faith & Simplicity Law Firm.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Hainan Yuexin Group Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 20 Haigang Road, Xiuying District, Haikou City, Hainan Province.
Legal Representative: Hong Jinsong, Chairman of the Company.
Agent ad litem: Yang Jiawen, lawyer of Fujian Weisheng Law Firm.
Agent ad litem: Fu Xiaoliuting, lawyer of Beijing Zhongyin Law Firm.

The applicant for retrial, Xiamen Yuanchang Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Yuanchang Company), filed an application for retrial with this Court regarding its dispute over a commission contract with the respondent, Hainan Yuexin Group Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Yuexin Company), against the civil judgment (2017) Qiong Min Zhong No. 2 (hereinafter referred to as the original judgment) rendered by the Hainan High People's Court (hereinafter referred to as Hainan High Court). On December 27, 2017, this Court rendered the Civil Ruling (2017) Zui Gao Fa Min Shen No. 3368, ordering a retrial of this case. This Court formed a collegial panel according to law and heard the case in open session on March 26, 2018. The agents ad litem of Yuanchang Company, Yang Shaoyong and Chen Xuanwen, and the agents ad litem of Yuexin Company, Yang Jiawen and Fu Xiaoliuting, appeared in court for the proceedings. The trial of this case has now been concluded.

Yuanchang Company applied for retrial on the grounds that the original judgment fell under the circumstances provided in Article 200(6) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Civil Procedure Law), requesting: 1. To set aside the original judgment, and amend it to confirm that Yuanchang Company holds a claim against Yuexin Company in the amount of RMB 34 million and liquidated damages, and to confirm that RMB 20 million of that claim has been set off against Yuexin Company's claim of RMB 20 million against Yuanchang Company; 2. That Yuexin Company bear all litigation costs in this case. Facts and reasons: I. The original judgment erred in finding that Yuanchang Company's lawsuit was barred by the statute of limitations. 1. The original judgment mischaracterized the declaratory action as an action for payment, and its reasoning conflicted with the operative part of the judgment. Yuanchang Company's claims were to confirm that Yuexin Company had breached the "Letter of Undertaking" it issued, and to accordingly seek rescission of the commission for handling the military procedures required for developing Plot No. Nanmin Zi 2726A of the "Yuanchang Shanzhuang" project in Xiamen City, and the "Letter of Undertaking" signed on November 18, 2005; to confirm that Yuanchang Company holds a claim of RMB 34 million and liquidated damages against Yuexin Company; and to confirm that Yuanchang Company is entitled to use a portion of the above claim to set off the mutual monetary claims between the parties on an equal basis. Yuanchang Company did not petition for an order directing Yuexin Company to return the RMB 20 million commission fee. Therefore, Yuanchang Company's request for confirmation of its claim against Yuexin Company and partial set-off is not subject to the statute of limitations. Having affirmed Yuanchang Company's claim to RMB 20 million and liquidated damages, the original judgment erroneously dismissed Yuanchang Company's claims by reason of its failure to assert the claim within the two-year limitation period. 2. The original judgment erroneously determined that the limitation period for the return of the commission fee began on February 18, 2006. For over six years, from November 18, 2005, to November 29, 2011, neither Yuanchang Company nor Yuexin Company asserted their respective claims. This was not due to inaction in exercising rights, but because Yuanchang Company believed that its claims against Yuexin Company had already been set off. Yuanchang Company had not known or should not have known that its rights were infringed and thus failed to exercise them. It was not until June 26, 2014, when Yuexin Company sued Yuanchang Company in the enterprise loan dispute case, that Yuanchang Company became aware of the infringement of its rights. Although Yuanchang Company did not assert the return of the commission fee, according to Article 137 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the General Principles of Civil Law), which provides that "the limitation of action begins when the person knows or should know that his rights have been infringed," the limitation period in this case should begin from the date Yuanchang Company received the complaint in the enterprise loan dispute case. 3. The original judgment's finding that Yuanchang Company's lawsuit was barred by the statute of limitations violates the legislative intent of the statute of limitations system. There is no factual basis that Yuanchang Company failed to exercise its rights after learning of the infringement. Moreover, before Yuexin Company sued Yuanchang Company in the enterprise loan dispute case, Yuanchang Company actively exercised its right of set-off through its defense, correspondence, and counterclaim, which confirms that Yuanchang Company was not dilatory. 4. The disparity in the application of the statute of limitations in the enterprise loan dispute case and the commission contract dispute case is severe. In the enterprise loan dispute case, Yuexin Company's claim was broadly held not to be time-barred and was protected; in the commission contract dispute case, Yuanchang Company's claim was strictly held to be time-barred and dismissed. II. The original judgment erred in finding that the debts between Yuanchang Company and Yuexin Company had not been set off. 1. The exercise of the right of set-off is not subject to time limits. The original judgment erred in finding that the set-off was not established because Yuanchang Company failed to present evidence that it had notified Yuexin Company of the debt set-off before the company surplus distribution dispute case. 2. The original judgment erred in finding that the set-off was not established because Yuexin Company's claim against Yuanchang Company was uncertain and the amount of the claim was not confirmed before the judgment in the enterprise loan dispute case. In the enterprise loan dispute case, Yuanchang Company never denied its obligation to Yuexin Company in the amount of RMB 20 million; it only asserted that this obligation had been set off against the commission fee Yuexin Company was required to return to Yuanchang Company. Therefore, there is no factual basis that Yuexin Company's claim against Yuanchang Company was uncertain. Furthermore, when Yuanchang Company filed its defense in the company surplus distribution dispute case initiated by Yuexin Company in 2011, it had already notified Yuexin Company that the mutual debts had been set off. 3. The original judgment deliberately overlooked the provision in the "Letter of Undertaking" that Yuanchang Company has the right to elect to set off against Yuexin Company's debts. In the "Letter of Undertaking," Yuexin Company explicitly promised to complete the entrusted matters by January 28, 2006; otherwise, it would fully refund the total commission fee of RMB 20 million to Yuanchang Company and Hou Changcai by February 18, 2006. If the refund was overdue, Hou Changcai would choose other methods of disposal. Yuexin Company failed to complete the entrusted matters and should refund the commission fee of RMB 20 million to Yuanchang Company. Yuanchang Company could elect to set off its claim for that RMB 20 million commission fee against its obligation to Yuexin Company for the remaining investment amount of RMB 20 million in the Quanzhou Donghai Tantan Rectification Project. In summary, Yuanchang Company and Yuexin Company owed mutual debts. Apart from sending a letter on December 31, 2014, clearly expressing the intention to set off, Yuanchang Company also notified Yuexin Company multiple times in the 2011 company surplus distribution dispute case, the 2014 enterprise loan dispute case, and in this case that the mutual debts had been set off. Pursuant to Article 99 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Contract Law), the mutual debts have been set off. The courts of first and second instance in this case found that Yuanchang Company's assertion of set-off was not established, which clearly violated the law.

Yuexin Company argued in defense: I. The "Letter of Undertaking" was not a unilateral commitment but a mutual agreement. The signature of Hou Changcai, the legal representative of Yuanchang Company, appeared in the witness column of the "Letter of Undertaking." Hou Changcai, who was also the party to whom the commitment was made, signed in the "witness" column, but it nevertheless represented the consent of one party to the agreement, i.e., acceptance of the contents of the "Letter of Undertaking," and knowledge of the starting point of the date of infringement. II. Yuanchang Company's claim for set-off cannot be established as a matter of law. Article 99 of the Contract Law does not provide whether a statutory right of set-off can be exercised with respect to a time-barred claim. Yuexin Company believes that a creditor cannot exercise the right of set-off on a time-barred claim. First, exercising the right of set-off on a time-barred claim would render the statute of limitations system meaningless. Second, allowing the exercise of a right of set-off on a time-barred claim is tantamount to compelling another person to perform a natural obligation. Third, the right of set-off should be exercised by notification within the limitation period. Fourth, Article 13 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Statute of Limitations in the Trial of Civil Cases provides: "The following matters shall be deemed by the people's court to have the same effect of interrupting the statute of limitations as filing a lawsuit: ... (8) asserting set-off in litigation ..." Thus, asserting set-off in litigation only has the effect of interrupting the statute of limitations, not automatically producing the effect of debt set-off. According to the "Letter of Undertaking," February 18, 2006, is the clear point of infringement. Pursuant to law, the two-year statute of limitations runs from February 18, 2006, to February 18, 2008. A creditor's assertion by themselves for repayment, assertion through litigation, or notification of set-off must be made within the statute of limitations to receive legal support. Yuanchang Company belatedly raised the issue of set-off after the statute of limitations had expired; thus, the set-off cannot be established as a matter of law. Moreover, Yuexin Company has repeatedly objected to Yuanchang Company's proposed set-off in two lawsuits; therefore, Yuanchang Company's set-off cannot be established. III. Yuanchang Company's claims in the first instance attempted to circumvent the statute of limitations issue for an action for payment by framing them as a declaratory action. Its indirect attempt to seek court support for a time-barred claim should not be sustained. IV. The period for exercising the right to rescind a contract is a statutory exclusion period. Yuanchang Company's claim for rescission of the contract exceeds the statutory period and should not be supported by the court. In conclusion, Yuexin Company argues that Yuanchang Company's claim for confirmation of its claim has exceeded the statute of limitations and should not be sustained; its claim for set-off cannot produce the effect of set-off through court support because its claim is a natural claim; and its claim for rescission of the contract has exceeded the statutory exclusion period and should not be sustained. Furthermore, Yuanchang Company's request in its retrial application to confirm that the commission fee claim of RMB 20 million has been set off against Yuexin Company's claim of RMB 20 million against Yuanchang Company exceeds the scope of its claims in the first instance and should be brought in a separate lawsuit.

Yuanchang Company's claims in the first instance: 1. To confirm that Yuexin Company breached the terms of its "Letter of Undertaking" by failing to obtain and transfer to Yuanchang Company by January 28, 2006, all procedures and documents (originals) of the Nanjing Military Region Logistics Department's transmittal of the General Logistics Department of the People's Liberation Army Document (2003) Hou Ying Zi No. 339 in the name of "Xiamen Longxiang Real Estate Development Co., Ltd." (hereinafter referred to as Longxiang Company); 2. To rescind the commission for handling the military procedures required for developing Plot No. Nanmin Zi 2726A of the "Yuanchang Shanzhuang" project in Xiamen City and the "Letter of Undertaking" signed on November 18, 2005, between Yuanchang Company and Yuexin Company; 3. To confirm that Yuanchang Company holds a claim against Yuexin Company in the amount of RMB 34 million and liquidated damages (calculated from April 13, 2005, for RMB 20 million; from April 14, 2005, for RMB 10 million; and from April 18, 2005, for RMB 4 million, all at four times the bank loan benchmark interest rate); 4. To confirm that Yuanchang Company is entitled to use a portion of the above claim to set off against the mutual monetary claims between Yuanchang Company and Yuexin Company on an equal basis; 5. That Yuexin Company bear all litigation costs in this case.

The Haikou Intermediate People's Court of Hainan Province (hereinafter referred to as Haikou Intermediate Court) found the following facts in the first instance: On November 18, 2005, Yuexin Company, as the promisor, issued a "Letter of Undertaking" to Yuanchang Company and Hou Changcai. The main contents were as follows: I, having been entrusted by your company and your good self on April 1, 2005, am responsible for handling the military procedures required for the development of Plot No. Nanmin Zi 2726A of the "Yuanchang Shanzhuang" project in Xiamen City (the specific entrusted matters being: I shall be responsible for applying in the name of the client to the Nanjing Military Region for the procedures and documents (originals) of the Nanjing Military Region Logistics Department's transmittal of the General Logistics Department of the People's Liberation Army Document (2003) Hou Ying Zi No. 339, and transfer them to your company, thereby completing the above entrusted matters. The client shall pay a total fee of RMB 30 million and two Mercedes-Benz sedans); I confirm that, as of April 13, 2005, I have successively received a commission fee of RMB 20 million from your company and your good self; I undertake to complete the entrusted matters by January 28, 2006. If I fail to complete the entrusted matters by January 28, 2006, I will fully refund the entire commission fee of RMB 20 million to Yuanchang Company and Hou Changcai by February 18, 2006. If the refund is overdue, Mr. Hou Changcai shall choose other methods of disposal. The "Letter of Undertaking" listed Yuexin Company as the promisor in the signature block, but Yuexin Company's corporate seal was not affixed. Signed on the document were Hong Jinsong and the witnesses Hou Changcai, Huang Jincheng, and Huang Yasam (signed on behalf by Huang Jincheng). On December 31, 2014, Yuanchang Company sent Yuexin Company a "Letter Regarding the Second Notice of Mutual Set-off of the RMB 20 Million Claims and Debts," stating that after it paid the relevant amounts to Yuexin Company, and because Yuexin Company neither completed the entrusted matters nor separately refunded the commission fee, it demanded that its claim of RMB 20 million against Yuexin Company be set off against Yuexin Company's claim of RMB 20 million against it. After the set-off, it would no longer owe any debt to Yuexin Company. Yuexin Company denied receiving the letter. Because Yuexin Company failed to repay the relevant amounts, Yuanchang Company filed this lawsuit with the Xiamen Intermediate People's Court on April 22, 2015. After the court accepted the case, Yuexin Company raised a jurisdictional objection. On July 15, 2015, the court rendered a Civil Ruling (2015) Xia Min Chu Zi No. 893, dismissing Yuexin Company's jurisdictional objection. Yuexin Company appealed the ruling to the Fujian High People's Court (hereinafter referred to as Fujian High Court). On December 4, 2015, Fujian High Court rendered a Civil Ruling (2015) Min Min Zhong Zi No. 1962, ruling to transfer the case to Haikou Intermediate Court for handling.

Separately, it was found: Hou Changcai paid RMB 5.05 million to Yuexin Company (including: RMB 2 million on April 11, 2005; RMB 1.25 million and RMB 1.8 million respectively on April 13, 2005); on April 14, 2005, Mingfa Group Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Mingfa Company) paid RMB 10 million to Yuexin Company; on April 18, 2005, Xiamen Yuanchang Urban Construction Group Co., Ltd. (formerly known as Fujian Yuanchang Engineering Construction Co., Ltd., hereinafter referred to as Yuanchang Urban Construction Company) paid RMB 4 million to Yuexin Company; the total of the above payments was RMB 19.05 million, and the purpose noted on each was "current account." Yuanchang Company submitted to the court payment instructions from Hou Changcai, Mingfa Company, and Yuanchang Urban Construction Company, all stating that the relevant amounts were paid on behalf of Yuanchang Company.

Further investigation: In 2005, Yuanchang Company and Yuexin Company negotiated matters regarding investment cooperation. On August 15, 2005, Yuexin Company remitted an investment fund of RMB 28,000,000 to Yuanchang Company's account. Subsequently, on October 26, 2005, Yuanchang Company returned an investment fund of RMB 8,000,000 to Yuexin Company. On November 29, 2011, Yuexin Company filed a lawsuit with the Fujian High People's Court on the grounds that the RMB 20,000,000 it had remitted to Yuanchang Company's account was an investment capital contribution to Yuanchang Company, and requested a judgment ordering Yuanchang Company to pay Yuexin Company undistributed investment equity of RMB 151,402,484. On June 16, 2012, the Fujian High People's Court issued Civil Judgment (2012) Min Min Chu Zi No. 1, holding that Yuexin Company's claim that it had invested RMB 20,000,000 in Yuanchang Company in 2005 lacked factual basis, and rendered a judgment dismissing Yuexin Company's claims. On August 15, 2012, Yuexin Company, dissatisfied with the judgment, filed an appeal, and later applied to withdraw the appeal during the second instance trial. On December 13, 2012, the Supreme People's Court issued Civil Ruling (2012) Min Er Zhong Zi No. 119, permitting Yuexin Company to withdraw the appeal. In 2013, Yuexin Company applied for retrial of Civil Judgment (2012) Min Min Chu Zi No. 1. The Supreme People's Court issued Civil Ruling (2013) Min Shen Zi No. 1374 on November 20, 2013, ruling: Yuexin Company's application for retrial is dismissed. On June 26, 2014, Yuexin Company filed a lawsuit with the Haikou Intermediate People's Court (cause of action: dispute over enterprise loan), requesting Yuanchang Company to return RMB 20,000,000 and interest. On December 26, 2014, Yuanchang Company filed a counterclaim, requesting: 1. To confirm that Yuanchang Company has a creditor's right based on the Letter of Commitment issued by Yuexin Company; 2. To confirm that Yuanchang Company is entitled to set off its creditor's right against its debt in accordance with the law and the terms of the Letter of Commitment issued by Yuexin Company; 3. To confirm that the creditor's rights and debts between Yuanchang Company and Yuexin Company have been mutually set off; 4. Yuexin Company to bear all litigation costs. On January 8, 2015, the court issued Civil Ruling (2014) Hai Zhong Fa Min Er Chu Zi No. 64-1, holding that Yuanchang Company's counterclaim was a dispute over an agency contract, while Yuexin Company's principal claim was a dispute over a loan contract; the two were not the same legal relationship nor based on the same legal facts, and accordingly ruled: Yuanchang Company's counterclaim is not accepted. Yuanchang Company, dissatisfied with the ruling, filed an appeal. The Hainan High People's Court issued Civil Ruling (2015) Qiong Li Yi Zhong Zi No. 94 on April 3, 2015, ruling: Appeal dismissed, original ruling affirmed. Subsequently, on December 29, 2015, the court rendered a judgment: 1. Yuanchang Company shall pay Yuexin Company RMB 20,000,000 and interest (interest calculation method: with RMB 20,000,000 as the principal, at an annual interest rate of 7%, calculated from November 29, 2011 to the date of performance as specified in the judgment); 2. Yuexin Company's other claims are dismissed. Yuanchang Company, dissatisfied with the judgment, appealed to the Hainan High People's Court. On July 26, 2016, the Hainan High People's Court rendered a judgment: Appeal dismissed, original judgment affirmed.

The Haikou Intermediate People's Court held at first instance: The issues in dispute between Yuanchang Company and Yuexin Company in this case are: 1. Whether Yuexin Company is a proper defendant in this case; 2. Whether Yuexin Company breached the contract and whether the contract in this case should be rescinded; 3. Whether Yuanchang Company has a creditor's right of RMB 34,000,000 and liquidated damages against Yuexin Company; 4. Whether Yuanchang Company has a right of set-off against Yuexin Company in this case; 5. Whether this case exceeds the statute of limitations.

First, regarding the issue of whether Yuexin Company is a proper defendant in this case. After Hou Changcai, Mingfa Company, and Yuanchang Urban Construction Company paid RMB 19,050,000 to Yuexin Company on behalf of Yuanchang Company, Hong Jinsong, the legal representative of Yuexin Company, issued a Letter of Commitment to Yuanchang Company and Hou Changcai in the name of Yuexin Company, and expressly specified the rights and obligations of the 'undersigned' in the letter. This is an act of a company's legal representative engaging in business activities in the name of the legal person, and the consequences of such act shall be borne by the legal person. Therefore, 'I' or the 'undersigned' in the Letter of Commitment should be Yuexin Company. Hence, Yuexin Company is a proper defendant in this case. Yuexin Company's defense that the subject of the Letter of Commitment was Hong Jinsong personally, and that page 8 of Civil Judgment (2012) Min Min Chu Zi No. 1 of the Fujian High People's Court had explicitly found that it involved Hong Jinsong personally, and that Yuanchang Company could not possibly have a creditor's right against Yuexin Company, is inconsistent with the facts and is not adopted.

Second, regarding the issue of whether Yuexin Company breached the contract and whether the contract in this case should be rescinded. In this case, after Yuanchang Company prepaid the agency fee to Yuexin Company, Yuexin Company issued a Letter of Commitment to Yuanchang Company in the name of the 'undersigned', which was accepted by Yuanchang Company. Therefore, the Letter is legally binding on both parties, and a legal relationship of agency contract was established between them. In the Letter, Yuexin Company undertook that on April 1, 2005, it was entrusted by Yuanchang Company to handle the military procedures required for the development of Plot No. Nan Min Zi No. 2726A of the 'Yuanchang Villa' project in Xiamen City, and would transfer the relevant procedures and documents (originals) to Yuanchang Company by January 28, 2006. However, Yuexin Company neither delivered the relevant documents and file originals to Yuanchang Company before the expiration of the promised deadline, nor fully returned the entire agency fee to Yuanchang Company and Hou Changcai by February 18, 2006. Therefore, Yuexin Company's delayed performance of the contract resulted in the failure to achieve the purpose of the contract, constituting a fundamental breach. Pursuant to Article 94, paragraph (4) of the Contract Law of the PRC, Yuanchang Company's claim for rescission of the agency contract between itself and Yuexin Company regarding the handling of the military procedures required for the development of Plot No. Nan Min Zi No. 2726A of the 'Yuanchang Villa' project in Xiamen City and for rescission of the Letter of Commitment signed by the parties on November 18, 2005, is supported by facts and law and is hereby upheld. Yuexin Company argued that the Longxiang Company's development of the 'Yuanchang Villa' project had already commenced in 2011 and had obtained a pre-sale permit, that Hong Jinsong's main obligations had been completed before 2006, which was also the fundamental reason why Yuanchang Company had not demanded the return of funds from Hong Jinsong since February 28, 2006, and that Yuanchang Company filed this lawsuit after Yuexin Company filed a lawsuit in an attempt to evade its debts, which is contrary to basic fairness and good faith. However, as Yuexin Company failed to provide sufficient evidence during the proceedings to prove that it had completed the entrusted matters, the court does not adopt the above defenses.

Third, regarding the issue of whether Yuanchang Company has a creditor's right of RMB 34,000,000 and liquidated damages against Yuexin Company. With respect to the creditor's right of RMB 34,000,000, the remittance instructions and relevant bank remittance vouchers submitted by Yuanchang Company to this court from Hou Changcai, Mingfa Company, and Yuanchang Urban Construction Company show that from April 11 to May 18, 2005, Yuanchang Company paid a total of RMB 19,050,000 to Yuexin Company. In the Letter of Commitment dated November 18, 2005, Yuexin Company undertook that if it failed to deliver the relevant documents and file originals to Yuanchang Company by January 28, 2006, it should fully refund the entire agency fee of RMB 20,000,000 to Yuanchang Company by February 18, 2006. As to Yuanchang Company's claim that it has a creditor's right of RMB 34,000,000 against Yuexin Company, because Yuexin Company did not fully acknowledge it, only acknowledging RMB 19,050,000, and Yuanchang Company failed to submit all evidence of its payment of RMB 34,000,000 to Yuexin Company, the court determines that Yuanchang Company has a creditor's right of RMB 20,000,000 against Yuexin Company. The creditor's right for the excess amount is not supported. With respect to liquidated damages, as mentioned above, Yuexin Company's failure to deliver the relevant documents and file originals to Yuanchang Company before the expiration of the promised deadline, and its failure to fully refund the entire agency fee to Yuanchang Company and Hou Changcai by February 18, 2006, constituted a breach of contract, and it shall bear corresponding liability for breach. As to Yuanchang Company's claim for a creditor's right to liquidated damages, the claim was for RMB 20,000,000 from April 13, 2005, RMB 10,000,000 from April 14, 2005, and RMB 4,000,000 from April 18, 2005, all calculated at four times the bank's corresponding loan interest rate. In this regard, the court holds that although Yuexin Company undertook in the Letter of Commitment dated November 18, 2005 that if it failed to deliver the relevant documents and file originals to Yuanchang Company by January 28, 2006, it should fully refund the entire agency fee of RMB 20,000,000 to Yuanchang Company by February 18, 2006, Yuanchang Company had always believed that its creditor's right of RMB 20,000,000 against Yuexin Company had been set off against Yuexin Company's creditor's right of RMB 20,000,000 against Yuanchang Company, and therefore did not demand the return from Yuexin Company. It was only after Yuexin Company filed another lawsuit regarding its creditor's right of RMB 20,000,000 in loan against Yuanchang Company that Yuanchang Company claimed its rights in this court. Therefore, the calculation of liquidated damages should commence from the date Yuanchang Company claimed its rights, i.e., December 26, 2014, the date when Yuanchang Company filed the counterclaim in this case. Calculation method of liquidated damages: with RMB 20,000,000 as the principal, from December 26, 2014 to the date of full payment, calculated at 30% above the one-year loan interest rate of the People's Bank of China for the corresponding period. Liquidated damages for the excess part are not supported. Yuexin Company's partial defense that the subject of the Letter of Commitment was Hong Jinsong personally and that Yuanchang Company could not possibly have a creditor's right of RMB 34,000,000 and liquidated damages against Yuexin Company is untenable and is not adopted by the court.

Fourth, regarding the issue of whether Yuanchang Company has a right of set-off in this case. This case is a dispute over an agency contract. In this case, Yuanchang Company requests confirmation of its creditor's right against Yuexin Company. Since this creditor's right and Yuexin Company's loan creditor's right against Yuanchang Company do not belong to the same legal relationship, and Yuexin Company's loan creditor's right against Yuanchang Company has been adjudicated in a separate case, the court does not address Yuanchang Company's claim that part of the creditor's right involved in this case should be used to offset its debt to Yuexin Company. It may claim set-off during enforcement.

Fifth, the issue of whether this case exceeds the statute of limitations. Both parties owed each other RMB 20,000,000 for several years. Yuanchang Company always believed that its debt to Yuexin Company had been set off against Yuexin Company's debt to it, and therefore did not claim its rights against Yuexin Company. It was only after Yuexin Company filed a separate lawsuit on June 26, 2014 regarding its loan creditor's right of RMB 20,000,000 against Yuanchang Company that Yuanchang Company became aware that its rights had been infringed. Therefore, the statute of limitations in this case should be calculated from the date Yuanchang Company received the complaint in that case. Yuanchang Company filed this lawsuit with the Xiamen Intermediate People's Court on April 22, 2015, which did not exceed the statutory two-year statute of limitations. Yuexin Company's defense that the Letter of Commitment set the final repayment deadline as February 28, 2006, and that after Yuexin Company filed a lawsuit against Yuanchang Company in 2011, Yuanchang Company, in violation of good faith and basic fairness, claimed its rights against Yuexin Company, which was already five years after 2006 and had long exceeded the statute of limitations, is untenable and is not adopted.

In summary, pursuant to Articles 135 and 137 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the PRC, Article 94(4), Article 99(1), Articles 107 and 396 of the Contract Law of the PRC, and Article 64(1) of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, the judgment is as follows: Rescind the agency contract between Yuanchang Company and Yuexin Company for handling the military procedures required for the development of Plot No. Nan Min Zi No. 2726A of the 'Yuanchang Villa' project in Xiamen City and the Letter of Commitment signed by the parties on November 18, 2005; Confirm that Yuanchang Company has a creditor's right of RMB 20,000,000 and liquidated damages (with RMB 20,000,000 as the principal, calculated from December 26, 2014 to the date of full payment at 30% above the one-year loan interest rate of the People's Bank of China for the corresponding period) against Yuexin Company; Dismiss Yuanchang Company's other claims. Court acceptance fee of RMB 261,800 shall be borne by Yuanchang Company in the amount of RMB 96,866 and by Yuexin Company in the amount of RMB 164,934.

Yuanchang Company, dissatisfied with the first instance judgment, appealed to the Hainan High People's Court, requesting: 1. To amend item 2 of the first instance judgment, to confirm that Yuanchang Company has a creditor's right of RMB 34,000,000 and liquidated damages (of which RMB 20,000,000 from April 13, 2005, RMB 10,000,000 from April 14, 2005, and RMB 4,000,000 from April 18, 2005, all calculated at four times the bank's corresponding loan interest rate) against Yuexin Company; 2. To order Yuexin Company to bear all litigation costs of this case. Facts and reasons: I. The first instance court only found that Yuanchang Company had a creditor's right of RMB 20,000,000 and liquidated damages against Yuexin Company, while Yuanchang Company actually had a creditor's right of RMB 34,000,000 and liquidated damages. The finding of facts is erroneous. In the Letter of Commitment, Yuexin Company confirmed that as of April 13, 2005, it had successively received an agency fee of RMB 20,000,000. After April 13, 2005, Yuanchang Company, Mingfa Company, and Yuanchang Urban Construction Company remitted RMB 14,000,000 to Yuexin Company. Therefore, the RMB 14,000,000 was not included in the already confirmed RMB 20,000,000. The Letter of Commitment also states that 'for handling the aforementioned entrusted matters, the client shall pay a total fee of RMB 30,000,000 and two Mercedes-Benz cars,' which also corroborates that Yuanchang Company has a creditor's right of RMB 34,000,000 against Yuexin Company. Since the first instance court did not agree to Yuanchang Company's application to withdraw its claim regarding the RMB 14,000,000, as to the principal, the court should have found that Yuanchang Company had a creditor's right of RMB 34,000,000 against Yuexin Company, rather than only RMB 20,000,000. The first instance judgment's finding of facts on this point is erroneous and should be corrected by the appellate court. II. The first instance court erred in determining the start date for calculating the liquidated damages owed to Yuanchang Company, and the interest rate standard is clearly too low. Because Yuexin Company denied the set-off of the creditor's rights and debts, the first instance court determined that the liquidated damages should be calculated from the date Yuanchang Company claimed its rights, which is an erroneous start date. The interest rate standard, calculated at 30% above the one-year loan interest rate of the People's Bank of China for the corresponding period, is clearly too low. As stated above, the liquidated damages owed to Yuanchang Company should be calculated based on RMB 34,000,000, from the date the Letter of Commitment confirmed receipt of the funds and the date the funds were remitted, i.e., RMB 20,000,000 from April 13, 2005, RMB 10,000,000 from April 14, 2005, and RMB 4,000,000 from April 18, 2005, all at four times the bank's corresponding loan interest rate.

Yuexin Company argued in defense: I. Yuanchang Company does not have any creditor's right against Yuexin Company. 1. The first instance found that this case is a dispute over an agency contract, and Yuanchang Company's request in this case to confirm its creditor's right against Yuexin Company does not belong to the same legal relationship as Yuexin Company's loan creditor's right against Yuanchang Company. That is, Yuanchang Company's claimed right of set-off does not comply with the law. 2. According to Article 99 of the Contract Law of the PRC, set-off must require 'mutually owed matured debts,' 'same type and quality,' and 'issuance of a notice of set-off.' The effective Civil Judgment (2016) Qiong Min Zhong No. 154 of the Hainan High People's Court has already found that 'Yuanchang Company failed to produce evidence that it had issued a notice of set-off to Yuexin Company before Yuexin Company filed a lawsuit claiming profit distribution,' meaning that no legal effect of set-off occurs in this case. 3. The first instance judgment erroneously interrupted the statute of limitations based on Yuanchang Company's 'subjective self-perceived' 'illegal right of set-off.' Yuanchang Company does not have any creditor's right against Yuexin Company. First, the first instance judgment already found that Yuanchang Company's self-perceived right of set-off does not comply with the law. Second, Yuanchang Company did not take any specific act of set-off, but only made a unilateral 'subjective awareness' in its own statement. Third, based on the effective judgment of the Hainan High People's Court confirming the above facts, the first instance judgment again interrupted the statute of limitations on the grounds that Yuanchang Company believed it had a right of set-off, which is clearly erroneous. II. Yuanchang Company has no creditor's right against Yuexin Company at all, and the subject is wrong; its claim of RMB 34,000,000 is even more a malicious false lawsuit. First, the Letter of Commitment involved in the case was signed by 'Hong Jinsong personally' on November 18, 2005, and the ultimate purpose was the development of the 'Yuanchang Villa' project by Longxiang Company. That project had already commenced in 2011 and has obtained a pre-sale permit now. Hong Jinsong's main obligations had been completed long ago, which is also the fundamental reason why Yuanchang Company had not demanded the return of funds from Hong Jinsong since February 18, 2006. Yuanchang Company's claim for a creditor's right against Yuexin Company is not only a wrong subject, but also factually impossible. Second, because Yuanchang Company entrusted Hong Jinsong personally to handle the land procedures for the 'Yuanchang Villa' project, Yuanchang Company remitted a total of RMB 19,050,000 to Yuexin Company through Hou Changcai, Yuanchang Urban Construction Company, and Mingfa Company. There is no such amount as RMB 34,000,000 as stated in Yuanchang Company's claims. In the cases (2012) Min Min Chu Zi No. 1 heard by the Fujian High People's Court and (2014) Hai Zhong Fa Min Er Chu Zi No. 64 heard by the Haikou Intermediate People's Court, Yuanchang Company had always asserted that the actual remitted amount was RMB 19,050,000. Now, disregarding the basic facts and its own previous multiple statements, Yuanchang Company claims RMB 34,000,000 in this case, which is a false lawsuit contrary to basic good faith. In summary, this case is a false lawsuit filed by Yuanchang Company to evade debts. Yuanchang Company has no creditor's right against Yuexin Company at all, and its appeal requests are clearly unsustainable.

Yuexin Company's appeal request: 1. Revoke Items 1 and 2 of the first-instance judgment according to law, and amend the judgment to dismiss all claims of Yuanchang Company; 2. The litigation costs of the first and second instances in this case shall be borne by Yuanchang Company. Facts and grounds: I. Yuanchang Company's filing of this lawsuit has already exceeded the statute of limitations, and the first-instance judgment found the facts clearly in error. 1. The first-instance judgment has determined that the "Letter of Commitment" explicitly stipulated that the return time for the 20 million yuan involved in the case (even if it should be returned) was February 18, 2006, of which Yuanchang Company was clearly aware. 2. Prior to Yuexin Company's filing of the lawsuit in 2011, Yuanchang Company had never made any expression of intention or specific action regarding "set-off." The so-called "set-off" was merely Yuanchang Company's unilateral statement after Yuexin Company filed the lawsuit. In the absence of "evidence of set-off," the first-instance judgment had no choice but to find that Yuanchang Company "consistently believed" this, without any specific action or objective evidence. First, the "Letter of Commitment" does not contain any expression of intention regarding debt set-off. Second, during the five-year period from the signing of the 2006 "Letter of Commitment" until Yuexin Company filed the lawsuit in 2011, Yuanchang Company never made any expression of intention regarding debt set-off. In this regard, the effective Civil Judgment (2016) Qiong Min Zhong No. 154 of Hainan High People's Court has already found that "after Yuexin Company filed this lawsuit, Yuanchang Company issued the 'Letter on Again Notifying the Mutual Set-off of the 20 Million Yuan Creditor's Rights and Debts' on December 31, 2014" and "Yuanchang Company failed to adduce evidence to prove that it had issued a notice of debt set-off to Yuexin Company before Yuexin Company sued for profit distribution." 3. The first-instance judgment's finding that June 26, 2014, served as the starting point for the statute of limitations was clearly erroneous and contrary to common sense. The objective starting point of the statute of limitations of February 18, 2006, as stipulated in the "Letter of Commitment," was known to both parties. Whether the parties owed debts to each other was merely Yuanchang Company's unilateral statement, which Yuexin Company has never acknowledged; as for the set-off of the debts between the two parties, it has always been Yuanchang Company's unilateral "subjective perception" without any specific action or expression of intention to Yuexin Company, and Yuexin Company has consistently and resolutely refused to acknowledge it. II. Yuanchang Company has never claimed creditor's rights against Yuexin Company, and this case has already exceeded the statute of limitations. The substantive reason is that Yuanchang Company does not actually have any creditor's rights against Yuexin Company (Yuexin Company is an improper defendant). The main evidence for Yuanchang Company's filing of this lawsuit is the "Letter of Commitment" signed personally by Hong Jinsong on November 18, 2005. The ultimate purpose of Hong Jinsong's obligation under this "Letter of Commitment" was for Longxiang Company to develop the "Yuanchang Villa" project. This project had already commenced construction in 2011 and has since obtained a pre-sale permit. Hong Jinsong's main obligations were already fulfilled long ago, which is the fundamental reason why Yuanchang Company never demanded repayment from Hong Jinsong after February 18, 2006. Not only was Yuanchang Company's claim for creditor's rights against the wrong party, but in fact, it was impossible for Yuanchang Company to have any creditor's rights. In 2011, when Yuexin Company claimed a profit distribution of 20 million yuan from Yuanchang Company, after the court determined that the sum was not an investment, Yuexin Company again filed a lawsuit on the grounds of a loan dispute. To evade the 20 million yuan debt, Yuanchang Company asserted that it had a 20 million yuan creditor's right against Yuexin Company. After Yuexin Company claimed the principal of 20 million yuan plus over 10 million yuan in interest, Yuanchang Company then claimed that the amount of creditor's rights it held against Yuexin Company was 34 million yuan. The above content fully demonstrates that Yuanchang Company filed this lawsuit and, in bad faith and self-contradictorily, adjusted the amount of its claims, all solely to evade its debt to Yuexin Company, not because it genuinely held creditor's rights against Yuexin Company. The subjective malice is evident. III. It is clear that Yuanchang Company's filing of this lawsuit, contrary to basic facts and good faith, constitutes a false lawsuit. Because Yuanchang Company entrusted Hong Jinsong personally to handle the land procedures for the "Yuanchang Villa" project, Yuanchang Company remitted a total of 19.05 million yuan to Yuexin Company through the accounts of Hou Changcai, Yuanchang Urban Construction Company, and Mingfa Company. The 34 million yuan as stated in Yuanchang Company's claims simply does not exist. In Case No. (2012) Min Min Chu Zi No. 1 and Case No. (2014) Hai Zhong Fa Min Er Chu Zi No. 64, Yuanchang Company consistently asserted that the actual amount remitted was 19.05 million yuan. Now, in this case, claiming 34 million yuan constitutes a false lawsuit in violation of basic good faith.

Yuanchang Company argued in defense: The statute of limitations has not been exceeded in this case. I. Yuanchang Company's claim in the first instance was for rescission of the contract, which is not subject to a statute of limitations in this case. II. The prerequisite for set-off is that both parties owe monetary debts. The actual controllers of Yuexin Company and Yuanchang Company were sworn brothers, and they had previously discussed compensation matters after the set-off. III. In the previous judgment, Yuexin Company considered the creditor's right in this case to be unclear, and Yuanchang Company was unaware of the creditor's right. Yuanchang Company only became aware that Yuexin Company denied the set-off of the creditor's right in this case when Yuexin Company filed the lawsuit for profit distribution, and it explicitly proposed the set-off during the litigation. Therefore, Yuanchang Company believes that the starting point for the set-off should be calculated from the date it knew its rights were infringed upon, and the statute of limitations has not been exceeded in this case. IV. Hong Jinsong did not fulfill his original commitment obligations. The settlement of certain prior matters between the actual controllers of the two parties pertains to the settlement of subsequent payments. Based on the timing of the remittances and the "Letter of Commitment" issued by Yuexin Company, the subject matter of the dispute is 34 million yuan. Yuexin Company has already confirmed the 20 million yuan, and the remaining 14 million yuan was remitted after the issuance of the "Letter of Commitment." V. Yuanchang Company believes that the issuance of the "Letter of Commitment" was an act of Yuexin Company, executed by Hong Jinsong as the legal representative of Yuexin Company, and all funds were remitted into Yuexin Company's account. Based on the timing of the remittances and other factors, the subject matter of the dispute should be 34 million yuan, and Yuanchang Company's claims should be supported.

The second instance additionally found that on March 12, 2012, during the trial of Case No. (2012) Min Min Chu Zi No. 1, in the column for the object of proof of Evidence Nos. 10-13 in the list of evidentiary materials submitted by Yuanchang Company to the court, it was stated that Yuanchang Company had remitted a total of 19.05 million yuan to Yuexin Company through the accounts of Hou Changcai, Yuanchang Urban Construction Company, Mingfa Company, etc. Together with other payments made by Yuanchang Company to Yuexin Company, Yuexin Company later signed a supplementary "Letter of Commitment" confirming that it had successively received 20 million yuan in entrustment fees from Yuanchang Company regarding the "Yuanchang Villa" project. On December 16, 2014, during the trial of Case No. (2014) Hai Zhong Fa Min Er Chu Zi No. 64, in the column for the object of proof of Evidence Nos. 7-10 in the list of evidentiary materials submitted by Yuanchang Company to the court, it was stated that Yuanchang Company had remitted a total of 19.05 million yuan to Yuexin Company through the accounts of Hou Changcai, Yuanchang Urban Construction Company, Mingfa Company, etc. Together with other payments made by Yuanchang Company to Yuexin Company, the total payment was 20 million yuan, and Yuanchang Company held a 20 million yuan creditor's right against Yuexin Company.

Except for the above facts, other facts found in the second instance are consistent with those found in the first-instance judgment.

Hainan High People's Court held in the second instance that the focal issues in dispute in the second instance of this case are: 1. Whether Yuanchang Company holds creditor's rights against Yuexin Company and what the amount of such creditor's rights is. 2. Whether Yuanchang Company's filing of this lawsuit has exceeded the statute of limitations.

I. Regarding whether Yuanchang Company holds creditor's rights against Yuexin Company and the amount of such creditor's rights. Yuanchang Company appealed, claiming that it holds a 34 million yuan creditor's right against Yuexin Company. Yuexin Company argued in defense that the actual remittance from Yuanchang Company was 19.05 million yuan. This court holds that in this case, the bank transfer vouchers and remittance explanations provided by Yuanchang Company in support of its claims all show that Yuexin Company received 19.05 million yuan paid by Yuanchang Company from April 11 to May 18, 2005. After the remittance, on November 18, 2005, Yuexin Company confirmed in the "Letter of Commitment" that it had successively received 20 million yuan in entrustment fees and promised in Item 2 of the commitments that if the entrusted matters could not be completed by January 28, 2006, it would refund the 20 million yuan in entrustment fees collected to Yuanchang Company and Hou Changcai by February 18, 2006. In the lists of evidence submitted by Yuanchang Company to the court during the trials of Case No. (2012) Min Min Chu Zi No. 1 and Case No. (2014) Hai Zhong Fa Min Er Chu Zi No. 64, Yuanchang Company also indicated that it had remitted a total of 19.05 million yuan to Yuexin Company through the accounts of Hou Changcai, Yuanchang Urban Construction Company, Mingfa Company, etc., and together with other payments made by Yuanchang Company to Yuexin Company, the total payment was 20 million yuan. After receiving the 20 million yuan in entrustment fees paid by Yuanchang Company, Yuexin Company neither completed the entrusted matters as stipulated in the "Letter of Commitment" nor refunded the 20 million yuan in entrustment fees to Yuanchang Company in accordance with the "Letter of Commitment" by February 18, 2006. The first-instance judgment's finding that Yuanchang Company holds a 20 million yuan creditor's right against Yuexin Company has factual and legal basis. Yuanchang Company claims that it has paid 34 million yuan to Yuexin Company, but it has not provided all the evidence for the actual payment of 34 million yuan. Yuexin Company has also failed to provide counter-evidence to overturn the fact recorded in the "Letter of Commitment" that it had received 20 million yuan. Therefore, this court does not support the appeal claims of either Yuanchang Company or Yuexin Company on this issue. Furthermore, the promisor signed on the "Letter of Commitment" is Yuexin Company, and Hong Jinsong, the legal representative of Yuexin Company, signed the letter. Based on the evidence materials provided by both parties, the sums involved in the case were all paid to Yuexin Company. The first-instance judgment's finding that Yuexin Company is the proper defendant in this case is not improper. Yuexin Company's appeal claim that Yuanchang Company's assertion of creditor's rights against it constitutes an error in the party is unfounded and is not supported.

II. Regarding whether Yuanchang Company's filing of this lawsuit has exceeded the statute of limitations. Yuexin Company appealed, claiming that Yuanchang Company's filing of this lawsuit has already exceeded the statute of limitations. Yuanchang Company argued in defense that its claim for rescission of the contract is not subject to a statute of limitations and that Yuanchang Company has consistently believed that the 20 million yuan creditor's right in this case had been set off against another 20 million yuan creditor's right that Yuexin Company held against Yuanchang Company. Yuanchang Company only became aware that Yuexin Company denied the set-off of the creditor's right in this case when Yuexin Company filed the lawsuit for profit distribution. The statute of limitations for this case should begin to run from the date Yuexin Company filed the lawsuit for profit distribution, and the statute of limitations has not been exceeded in this case. In this regard, this court holds that Article 99 of the Contract Law stipulates: "Where the parties mutually owe mature debts, and the subject matter of the debts is of the same kind and quality, either party may set off its own debt against the debt of the other party, except as otherwise provided by law or as is not permitted by the nature of the contract. A party that claims set-off shall notify the other party. The notice becomes effective upon reaching the other party. Set-off shall not be subject to any conditions or time limits." Accordingly, set-off is an act of disposing of creditor's rights, and the creditor shall notify the debtor of its intention to set off, which becomes effective only upon the notice reaching the other party. In this case, although Yuanchang Company claims that the 20 million yuan creditor's right it holds against Yuexin Company has been set off against the 20 million yuan creditor's right that Yuexin Company holds against it, Yuanchang Company has no evidence to prove that it had issued a notice of debt set-off to Yuexin Company before Yuexin Company sued for profit distribution. Yuexin Company also denies ever receiving a notice of debt set-off from Yuanchang Company, denies that the parties reached any agreement on debt set-off, and the 20 million yuan creditor's right of Yuexin Company against Yuanchang Company was not yet determined prior to the issuance of Civil Judgment (2016) Qiong Min Zhong No. 154 by this court on July 26, 2016. Yuanchang Company's consistent belief that set-off had occurred was merely its subjective understanding; in reality, no set-off had occurred between the parties. Therefore, Yuanchang Company's claim that its 20 million yuan creditor's right was set off in equal amount against the monetary creditor's right and debt between it and Yuexin Company is not supported. In the "Letter of Commitment," Yuexin Company promised to complete the entrusted matters by January 28, 2006, and if it could not complete the entrusted matters by January 28, 2006, it would fully refund the 20 million yuan in entrustment fees to Yuanchang Company and Hou Changcai by February 18, 2006. After the issuance of the "Letter of Commitment," Yuexin Company failed to obtain and transfer to Yuanchang Company the original documents and materials required for the development of the land parcel for the "Yuanchang Villa" project in accordance with the "Letter of Commitment" by January 28, 2006. Yuexin Company should have refunded 20 million yuan to Yuanchang Company and Hou Changcai by February 18, 2006, but Yuexin Company failed to do so. Since February 18, 2006, Yuanchang Company knew that its rights had been infringed upon and should have claimed the return of the 20 million yuan entrustment fees from Yuexin Company. Pursuant to Article 135 of the General Principles of the Civil Law, the statute of limitations for this case should begin to run from February 18, 2006, and expired on February 18, 2008. Yuanchang Company did not claim the return of the 20 million yuan entrustment fees from Yuexin Company during this period, and it is not legally protected. Even if Yuanchang Company claims that it asserted set-off against Yuexin Company when Yuexin Company filed the profit distribution lawsuit in 2011, the statute of limitations had already expired. In summary, Yuanchang Company's filing of this lawsuit has exceeded the statute of limitations. The first-instance judgment found that Yuanchang Company had consistently believed that the debt it owed to Yuexin Company had been set off against the debt Yuexin Company owed to it, that Yuanchang Company only knew its rights had been infringed upon when Yuexin Company filed another lawsuit on June 26, 2014, and that Yuanchang Company's filing of this lawsuit on April 22, 2015, had not exceeded the statute of limitations. This finding was erroneous and should be corrected.

Regarding Yuanchang Company's request for a judgment to rescind its entrustment with Yuexin Company and the "Letter of Commitment." In this case, the "Letter of Commitment" is a letter unilaterally issued by Yuexin Company to Yuanchang Company. Based on its content, it only imposes obligations on Yuexin Company unilaterally and is not an agreement defining the rights and obligations of both parties in the usual sense. The "Letter of Commitment" stipulates that if Yuexin Company fails to complete the entrusted matters by January 28, 2006, Yuexin Company must refund the 20 million yuan entrustment fees to Yuanchang Company by February 18, 2006; if the refund is overdue, the legal representative of Yuanchang Company, Hou Changcai, may choose other disposal methods. From the actual performance, when Yuexin Company failed to obtain and transfer to Yuanchang Company the original documents and materials required for the development of the land parcel for the "Yuanchang Villa" project in accordance with the "Letter of Commitment" by January 28, 2006, it had already indicated through its actual conduct that it would no longer perform the matters it had promised to handle for Yuanchang Company. Yuanchang Company could only demand the return of 20 million yuan or choose other disposal methods in accordance with the contract. As stated above, Yuanchang Company neither requested a refund from Yuexin Company nor chose other methods of disposal, and the statute of limitations has already expired. Yuanchang Company's further request for a judgment to rescind its entrustment with Yuexin Company and the "Letter of Commitment" has no legal basis. The first-instance judgment's rescission of Yuanchang Company's "Letter of Commitment" to Yuexin Company was improper and should be corrected.

In conclusion, Yuexin Company's appeal claim is established and is supported. Yuanchang Company's claims are not established and are not supported. Pursuant to Articles 135 and 137 of the General Principles of the Civil Law and Article 170, Paragraph 1, Item 2 of the Civil Procedure Law, the judgment is as follows: 1. Revoke Civil Judgment (2016) Qiong 01 Min Chu No. 152 of Haikou Intermediate People's Court; 2. Dismiss Yuanchang Company's claims. The first-instance case acceptance fee is 261,800 yuan. The second-instance case acceptance fee of 164,934 yuan prepaid by Yuexin Company and the second-instance case acceptance fee of 96,866 yuan prepaid by Yuanchang Company shall be borne by Yuanchang Company.

During the retrial of this case, none of the parties submitted new evidence to this court.

The facts found in this retrial are consistent with the facts found in the original trial.

This court holds that, considering the opinions of the parties, the focal issues in dispute in this retrial are: 1. How should the amount of Yuanchang Company's creditor's rights against Yuexin Company be determined; 2. Whether Yuanchang Company's request to confirm the creditor's rights has exceeded the statute of limitations; 3. Whether Yuanchang Company can claim set-off with Yuexin Company's debt.

I. Regarding how the amount of Yuanchang Company's creditor's rights against Yuexin Company should be determined

Based on the facts found in the original judgment, the bank transfer vouchers and remittance explanations provided by Yuanchang Company in support of its claims all show that Yuexin Company received 19.05 million yuan paid by Yuanchang Company from April 11 to May 18, 2005. After the remittance, on November 18, 2005, Yuexin Company confirmed in the "Letter of Commitment" that it had successively received 20 million yuan in entrustment fees and promised that if it could not complete the entrusted matters by January 28, 2006, it would refund the 20 million yuan entrustment fees collected to Yuanchang Company and Hou Changcai by February 18, 2006. In the lists of evidence submitted by Yuanchang Company to the court during the trials of Case No. (2012) Min Min Chu Zi No. 1 and Case No. (2014) Hai Zhong Fa Min Er Chu Zi No. 64, Yuanchang Company also indicated that it had remitted a total of 19.05 million yuan to Yuexin Company through the accounts of Hou Changcai, Yuanchang Urban Construction Company, Mingfa Company, etc., and together with other payments made by Yuanchang Company to Yuexin Company, the total payment was 20 million yuan. After receiving the 20 million yuan in entrustment fees paid by Yuanchang Company, Yuexin Company neither completed the entrusted matters nor refunded the 20 million yuan entrustment fees in accordance with the "Letter of Commitment." The original judgment's finding that Yuanchang Company holds a 20 million yuan creditor's right against Yuexin Company has factual and legal basis. Yuanchang Company's claim that it has paid 34 million yuan to Yuexin Company lacks relevant evidence of actual payment. Yuanchang Company's claim that the original judgment erroneously determined the amount of creditor's rights is unsustainable and is not supported by this court.

II. Regarding whether Yuanchang Company's request to confirm the creditor's rights has exceeded the statute of limitations

As stated above, Yuanchang Company and Yuexin Company had actually reached a consensus that if the entrusted matters could not be completed, Yuexin Company should return the relevant entrustment fees before a certain deadline. Therefore, Yuanchang Company had the right to assert its rights against Yuexin Company when that deadline arrived on February 18, 2006, and the statute of limitations began to run from that date. Yuanchang Company's claim that it only became aware that its rights had been infringed upon after Yuexin Company sued it on June 26, 2014, and that the statute of limitations in this case should begin to run from the date it received the complaint in Case No. (2014) Hai Zhong Fa Min Er Chu Zi No. 64 filed by Yuexin Company, is clearly inconsistent with the provision in the statute of limitations system that when a performance period can be determined, the statute of limitations period shall be calculated from the date the performance period expires. Yuanchang Company's filing of this lawsuit to confirm the creditor's rights has exceeded the statute of limitations, and the original judgment's finding on this issue is not improper.

III. Regarding whether Yuanchang Company can claim set-off with Yuexin Company's debt

Although the active creditor's right held by Yuanchang Company against Yuexin Company has exceeded the statute of limitations, whether a set-off can be claimed for an active creditor's right that has already exceeded the statute of limitations depends on the analysis of the following issues: First, the formation of Yuanchang Company's right of set-off; Second, the exercise of Yuanchang Company's right of set-off.

(1) Regarding the formation of Yuanchang Company's right of set-off

The statutory right of set-off, as a right of formation, can arise as long as the conditions stipulated by law are met. Article 99, Paragraph 1 of the Contract Law sets forth the conditions for the formation of a statutory right of set-off, namely, where the parties mutually owe mature debts and the subject matter of the debts is of the same kind and quality, either party may set off its own debt against the debt of the other party, except as otherwise provided by law or as is not permitted by the nature of the contract.

1. With respect to the positive conditions for the formation of the right, statutory set-off requires that the parties owe debts to each other, that both debts are due, and that the subject matter is of the same kind and quality. Among these, the condition that both debts are due should be understood as follows: First, both debts have reached the performance period, i.e., they are in a state capable of being performed. Second, the time periods for each debt from the date performance becomes due to the expiration of the statute of limitations should overlap. That is to say, for the claim whose statute of limitations expires first, the other party's claim must have become due before the expiration of that claim's statute of limitations; for the claim whose statute of limitations expires later, at the time its performance becomes due, the statute of limitations for the other party's claim must not have yet expired. Within the overlapping segment of the above time periods, both claims are in a performable state without a statute of limitations defense, and the condition that "both debts are due" is satisfied. Even if, at the time the set-off right is subsequently exercised, the active claim has already exceeded the statute of limitations, this does not affect the establishment of this condition. Conversely, if there is no overlap in the above time periods, meaning that when the statute of limitations for one party's claim expires, the other party's claim has not yet entered the performance period, then when the former claim becomes performable, the other party may defend on the ground that its own claim has not yet become due; when the latter claim becomes performable, the other party may defend on the ground that its own claim has already exceeded the statute of limitations. In such a case, the claims of both parties are not simultaneously in a performable state without the above defenses. Even if, at the time the set-off right is subsequently exercised, the latter debt has entered the performance period, it is difficult to consider the condition satisfied. Since the defense of statute of limitations for a passive claim can be voluntarily waived by the party concerned, it can be determined that, when examining the positive conditions for the formation of the set-off right, primary consideration should be given to the statute of limitations of the active claim. That is, if the passive claim enters the performance period before the statute of limitations for the active claim expires, the condition that both debts are due should be deemed satisfied; otherwise, the condition cannot be deemed satisfied.

In this case, Yuanchang Company and Yuexin Company owe monetary debts to each other. Regarding the issue of both debts being due, Yuanchang Company holds a claim of RMB 20 million against Yuexin Company due to Yuexin Company's failure to complete the entrusted matters, with the performance period due on February 18, 2006. As for Yuexin Company's claim against Yuanchang Company, based on the facts found in the Hainan High People's Court (2016) Qiong Min Zhong No. 154 civil judgment, Yuanchang Company, in accordance with the "Minutes of the Shareholders' Meeting" dated November 18, 2005, promised to refund RMB 20 million to Yuexin Company. Since the minutes did not specify a time for the refund, pursuant to Article 62, Paragraph 4 of the Contract Law, Yuexin Company could demand the refund from Yuanchang Company at any time. From this, it can be determined that during the period from February 18, 2006, when Yuanchang Company's claim of RMB 20 million against Yuexin Company became due, to February 17, 2008, when its statute of limitations expired, Yuexin Company's claim of RMB 20 million against Yuanchang Company was also in a performable state. Therefore, both debts were due. In summary, Yuanchang Company and Yuexin Company owed each other due monetary debts, and the positive conditions for the formation of the statutory set-off right in this case have been established.

2. With respect to the negative conditions for the formation of the right, Article 99, Paragraph 1 of the Contract Law explicitly states that set-off is excluded if it is prohibited by law or by the nature of the contract. In this case, the parties owe each other monetary debts arising from a commission contract and a loan contract. These debts are not of a type prohibited by law or by the nature of the contract from being set off. As for the issue of setting off a claim that has exceeded the statute of limitations, this falls within the scope of examination of the positive conditions for the formation of the right and will not be repeated here.

In summary, according to Article 99, Paragraph 1 of the Contract Law, before the statute of limitations expired for Yuanchang Company's claim of RMB 20 million in commission fees against Yuexin Company, Yuanchang Company and Yuexin Company already owed each other due monetary debts, meeting the requirements for statutory set-off. Therefore, Yuanchang Company's set-off right was established.

(B) Concerning the Exercise of Yuanchang Company's Set-off Right

Article 99, Paragraph 2 of the Contract Law provides for the exercise of the statutory set-off right, i.e., a party that intends to assert set-off shall notify the other party. The notice becomes effective upon reaching the other party. Set-off shall not be subject to conditions or a time limit. Thus, it can be determined that notice is merely the method of exercising the statutory set-off right. Whether the party exercises the set-off right and notifies the other party promptly after the right is established does not affect the establishment of the right itself. In this case, although Yuanchang Company's exercise of the set-off right occurred after the statute of limitations had expired, this does not preclude the prior establishment of the set-off right. The notice of set-off is also a unilateral expression of intent. As long as the expression of intent reaches the other party, it can produce the legal effect of set-off without requiring the other party's consent. As a right of formation, the exercise of the set-off right is not subject to the statute of limitations. Therefore, the mutual debts of RMB 20 million between the parties in this case were already set off when Yuanchang Company informed Yuexin Company of the purpose of providing evidence regarding the set-off of debts in the (2012) Min Min Chu Zi No. 1 case. The original judgment's refusal to recognize the set-off on the grounds that Yuanchang Company's assertion of set-off had exceeded the statute of limitations and that Yuexin Company's claim was uncertain before the Hainan High People's Court rendered the (2016) Qiong Min Zhong No. 154 civil judgment lacks legal basis. Furthermore, since parties in a set-off relationship each owe a debt to the other, which to some extent serves as security for their own claims, the Contract Law of China does not impose a statute of repose on the exercise of the set-off right. Instead, it provides that after the set-off right holder exercises the set-off right, the other party may raise an objection within a certain period. However, even so, the exercise of the set-off right should not be unreasonably delayed. In this case, Yuexin Company and Yuanchang Company incurred monetary debts of equal amount at almost the same time at the end of 2005. Over a period of six years, neither party asserted a corresponding claim. After Yuexin Company filed the corporate profit distribution lawsuit (2012) Min Min Chu Zi No. 1 with the Fujian High People's Court in 2011, Yuanchang Company promptly asserted its claim for debt set-off in that case. This constitutes an assertion of rights within a reasonable period and can hardly be considered a failure to exercise the set-off right. Additionally, from the perspective of substantive fairness, if Yuanchang Company were denied the ability to exercise the set-off right on the ground that its claim had exceeded the statute of limitations, this would not only violate the legislative intent of the set-off right but also contradict the principle of fairness in civil law. In summary, Yuanchang Company's exercise of the set-off right in separate litigation was not improper, and the mutual claims have been set off.

Additionally, Yuanchang Company's first-instance claim sought confirmation of its right to set off monetary debts in equal amounts with Yuexin Company, while its retrial request sought confirmation that the mutual debts of RMB 20 million had already been set off. These two claims are slightly different. However, given that Yuanchang Company has the right to set off and has already sent a notice of set-off to Yuexin Company by informing it of the purpose of providing evidence in the (2012) Min Min Chu Zi No. 1 case, the set-off has indeed taken effect. Therefore, although Yuanchang Company's first-instance claim and retrial request are slightly different, this does not affect the substantive outcome of this case. Yuexin Company's request that Yuanchang Company file a separate lawsuit on the grounds that the retrial request exceeds the first-instance claim is not supported.

In conclusion, Yuanchang Company's request regarding the set-off of the mutual due debts of RMB 20 million between itself and Yuexin Company is established, and this court supports it. The other retrial requests are not established and are not supported by this court. Pursuant to Article 135 and Article 137 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China, Article 62, Paragraph 4 and Article 99 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, and Article 207, Paragraph 1 and Article 170, Paragraph 1, Item 2 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the judgment is as follows:

1. Revoke the (2017) Qiong Min Zhong No. 2 civil judgment of the Hainan High People's Court;
2. Revoke the (2016) Qiong 01 Min Chu No. 152 civil judgment of the Haikou Intermediate People's Court, Hainan Province;
3. Confirm that the mutual due debts of RMB 20 million between Xiamen Yuanchang Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. and Hainan Yuexin Group Co., Ltd. have been set off;
4. Dismiss the other claims of Xiamen Yuanchang Real Estate Development Co., Ltd.

Court acceptance fee for the first instance: RMB 261,800, of which Xiamen Yuanchang Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. shall bear RMB 96,866 and Hainan Yuexin Group Co., Ltd. shall bear RMB 164,934. Court acceptance fee for the second instance: RMB 261,800, of which Xiamen Yuanchang Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. shall bear RMB 96,866 and Hainan Yuexin Group Co., Ltd. shall bear RMB 164,934.

This judgment is final.
